purpose_of_this_fixture: Calibration fixture for A15, the handed-over package: five recordings from another seller, taken in as one set, graded once and blueprinted once. The client is a print and sign shop; the handing-over seller (Clodagh Rennard) ran a discovery call, two demos, an internal call review with no client present, and a pricing call, with her sales engineer (Kofi Danquah) on the demos and the review. The user attended none of them. The export grammar is a call-recording platform's: a metadata block with a claimed roster and machine-written highlights, topic dividers, and 'Speaker Name · mm:ss' label lines each followed by one text line; none of s1 to s23 carries it. The file names are recording ids that are not in date order; the dates sit inside the files, and two files share a date. The set plants: (1) a client figure the handing-over seller re-quotes three times as settled ('Wade said reprints are forty thousand a year') when the client's own words were 'around forty thousand?' with 'I'd want her to check that before anyone writes it down'; (2) a cross-call, cross-speaker conflict on reprint frequency between the discovery call (Gwen: six, seven a week) and the second demo (Wade: two, maybe three a week; Gwen: five last week), which the seller resolves in the room by picking a side; (3) in the first demo, two client speakers who agree on the facts ('We're not disagreeing. A job's got pieces.') and need different structures for them, which is a fork and not a conflict; the seller's team then picks a side internally. The repair asserted: the set is ordered by the dates in the files and by internal evidence (the same-day tie broken by 'this morning's demo'), never by file name or recording id; each summary records who was in the call from voices heard against the claimed roster, with provenance 'handed-over'; the re-quotes are recorded in the meeting register as 'second-hand' and never as client evidence, with the client's hedged original standing at its true location; both statements of the reprint conflict are kept with call, speaker and location as kind 'conflict', with no recency rule, no superseded entry and no arithmetic, and the seller's 'We'll go with Wade's number for now' is not adopted; the pieces disagreement is recorded as a fork with its two options and constituencies, open on the approval card, and the freeze proceeds with that element unbuilt until it is settled [L14]; the call review carries no client evidence and its platform claims go to the claims store and the corrections block; the pricing call's figures go through the audience rule; and discovery-check and the blueprint run once over the whole set rather than from the last call. It also carries names and figures narrated inside the seller's own screen share, quarantined, and a price objection that follows a stated price, the first in the set. Guards reversals R6 (a cross-speaker conflict is never resolved by recency) and R7 (a structural disagreement is a fork, not a conflict).
transcript_format: Five plain-text exports from a call-recording platform, one per recording, UTF-8 with three non-ASCII characters (the middle dot in label lines and the box-drawing rules). Each file opens with a metadata block between two rules: Recording (title), Recording ID, Date (YYYY-MM-DD), Duration, Host, Participants (a semicolon list from the meeting's invite and join records, including 'Notetaker (recording assistant)', a bot), Transcript ('automatic, en-US; speaker labels from meeting accounts') and three machine-written Highlights bullets. The body is topic sections opened by a divider line '── Title ──', and turns as a label line 'Speaker Name · mm:ss' followed by exactly one text line; no end times; no blank line between turns. Speaker labels come from the meeting accounts, so the roster's display names differ from the labels in two files (Gwendolyn Tarrant / Gwen Tarrant, Guadalupe Arrieta / Lupe Arrieta). By file, in the confirmed order: rec-4418-discovery.txt, 2026-07-14, 33:30, 391 lines, 173 turns, about 3,565 spoken words, client share 73% (Wade 33%, Gwen 22%, Jesse 18%), the seller's longest turn 91 words at 31:25 (the playback) and the client's 109 at 23:39; rec-4402-first-look.txt, 2026-07-23, 15:29, 212 lines, 91 turns, about 1,590 words, client share 28% (Kofi alone 54%, longest 93 words at 05:27 inside his screen share); rec-4431-internal-review.txt, 2026-07-23, 05:28, 92 lines, 34 turns, about 540 words, seller side only; rec-4397-production-walkthrough.txt, 2026-08-06, 12:12, 187 lines, 77 turns, about 1,230 words, client share 44% (Kofi 36%, longest 106 words at 01:14); rec-4409-pricing.txt, 2026-08-19, 10:02, 156 lines, 63 turns, about 1,000 words, client share 46% (the seller 54%, longest 109 words at 02:46, the scope read-back). Artefacts are few, as an automatic export tends to be: [laughs] x2, [inaudible] x1 and one '...' self-interruption in rec-4418, [crosstalk] x1 in rec-4397, and one turn cut off by an interruption with a trailing ' --' in rec-4409 (05:29). The ordinary mess of an automatic export is present without announcing itself: fillers ('um' x12, 'uh' x2, 'you know' x2 across the set), stutters and false starts ('I'm not, I'm not', 'the, the building'), two contractions written as 'gonna' and 'gotta', and three misheard names, 'Pen Hollow' for the client (rec-4418 02:27), 'Coffee' for the sales engineer (rec-4402 14:50) and 'Burn' for the co-owner (rec-4397 09:36), each recorded in intake.recognition_errors. No evidence quote spans an added filler, a stutter or a misheard name (the two stutters quoted in this sentence are examples, not evidence); where a quoted turn carries one, it sits outside the marks. Dates are stated in the files: Tuesday 14 July, Thursday 23 July (twice), Thursday 6 August and Wednesday 19 August 2026; the next step is Thursday 27 August at 9:00; no time zone is stated anywhere. Every location in this key is 'rec-NNNN, mm:ss Speaker Name (role)', from the label line the quoted text line sits under, with the two seller-side speakers carrying 'seller' and 'sales engineer' as their roles; the same convention is used in the intake block. The file names are cited by recording id in locations and by full name in the intake block's file list.
